# Known vulnerable Python dependencies of apps/api, as resolved from requirements.txt on 2026-09-30.
# pip-audit reports no severity, so EVERY advisory is listed, not only the serious ones.
# Regenerate: pip-audit -r apps/api/requirements.txt -f json -o r.json; then
#   python3 apps/api/scripts/ci/audit_gate.py --kind pip --report r.json --baseline /dev/null --print-baseline
#
# Every line below is an EXPOSURE THE PRODUCT CARRIES TODAY, written down so the audit gate
# can tell a newly published advisory (or a newly pinned vulnerable version) from a standing
# one. It is NOT a judgement that the advisory is harmless, and nothing here is "accepted risk"
# in the sense of somebody having decided to live with it: the upgrades are engineering-03's.
#
# THIS FILE MAY ONLY SHRINK. When a dependency is upgraded, delete its lines; the gate prints
# which lines have gone stale. Adding a line is a decision and belongs in a review with the
# reason written beside it. apps/api/scripts/ci/audit_gate.py is the reader and explains why
# the gate is a ratchet instead of "fail on anything".
#
# Format: one advisory id per line, then `# package version [severity] - title (fix: ...)`.
